chain.label: Ambiguous glideslope/fast-slow indicator design
chain.trigger: the glideslope and fast/slow indicators are the same color and about the same size; the glideslope indicator is only visible when a valid ILS frequency has been selected

chain.label: First officer delayed switching to ILS frequency
chain.trigger: the first officer did not switch the VHF NAV receivers from the HUB VOR frequency to the ILS frequency until the airplane was at an altitude of about 1,000 feet

chain.label: Flight crew unable to activate APR mode
chain.trigger: neither the first officer nor the captain was initially able to activate the APR mode on their flight directors

caused_by.evidence: An ILS frequency must be selected as the NAV source and valid ILS signals must be received for the APR mode to activate

chain.label: Pilots mistook fast/slow indicator for glideslope indicator
chain.trigger: the pilots most likely mistook the fast/slow indicator for the glideslope indicator throughout the approach sequence

caused_by.evidence: the fast/slow indicator would have remained visible on the EADI even after the ILS frequency was selected, which may explain why the pilots did not immediately notice the glideslope indicator deviation
the first officer's failure to activate and identify the ILS frequency earlier in the approach prevented the flight crew from recognizing that the airplane was off course and below the glideslope

chain.label: Airplane descended well below glideslope uncorrected
chain.trigger: the airplane was actually about 700 feet below the glideslope when the first officer made these statements, and the airplane remained well below the glideslope throughout the rest of the approach

caused_by.evidence: ‘we're high on the glideslope now’ ... ‘yeah you're on [the] glideslope now’

chain.label: First officer switched NAV frequency without informing captain
chain.trigger: the first officer switched the frequency of a primary navigational aid and failed to inform the captain

caused_by.evidence: the first officer did not switch the VHF NAV receivers ... until the airplane was at an altitude of about 1,000 feet

chain.label: GPWS failed to generate expected alerts
chain.trigger: the CVR did not record the accident GPWS generate any alerts during the flight ... the Safety Board was unable to determine why the GPWS did not operate as expected

chain.label: Flight crew failed to execute a missed approach
chain.trigger: the CVR did not record either pilot call for a missed approach or initiate a go-around

caused_by.evidence: about the time that the airplane was at an altitude of about 500 feet, the glideslope display would have shown a deviation of more than one dot and the descent rate would have exceeded 1,000 fpm
because the airplane was at such a low altitude (about 1,000 feet) in IMC, such a major change should have prompted the captain to immediately initiate a missed approach
the ‘glideslope,’ ‘500’ foot, ‘too low terrain,’ ‘minimums,’ ‘300’ foot, and ‘200’ foot GPWS alerts should have activated on the accident flight

chain.label: Airplane struck light pole and crashed
chain.trigger: the airplane impacted a light pole at an altitude of about 198 feet and about 3 1/4 miles from the runway 4 threshold

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew failed to follow approved company approach procedures ... compliance ... would likely have prevented the accident
the airplane remained 600 to 1,000 feet below the glideslope until impact

chain.label: Fatal injuries to occupants; minor injury on ground
chain.trigger: the two pilots and the flight attendant were killed, an individual in a vehicle near the airport received minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was destroyed by impact forces
